issues.description: The frame carries a FrameProcessor reference where an id or name would do.
issues.detail: Putting a live FrameProcessor object on a control frame is heavier than the problem requires. The receiver only needs to know 'is this for me?' A string id, name, or weakref would let the frame stay a plain data structure that can be logged, compared, and serialized without dragging the whole processor graph along. Data dominates: pick the smallest shape that answers the question.

issues.description: Identity-by-equality on FrameProcessor is fragile; use `is` or an id.
issues.detail: `frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on whatever __eq__ FrameProcessor inherits. For object identity the idiom is `is`. Better still: compare ids. Right now a future __eq__ override on FrameProcessor silently changes routing semantics. Small data, explicit comparison.

issues.description: Suppression rule no longer covers inactive-service request frames.
issues.detail: Old code dropped every RequestMetadataFrame at the switcher boundary. New code only drops the one targeting the active service. If a request frame targeting an inactive service somehow reaches push_frame, it now leaks downstream. Today the dispatcher only sends to the active service, so it cannot happen — but the invariant is implicit. Either assert it or drop all of them.

issues.description: STTService and mock now duplicate the same handle-then-forward pattern.
issues.detail: Both services do `_push_metadata(); push_frame(frame)` for ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame. That is a small composable shape — a base ServiceMetadataEmitter mixin or a one-line helper on the base class would prevent every future service from rediscovering the contract (handle, then forward so siblings can also handle). Not urgent, but the duplication will grow.

review.summary: Small, focused rename plus a useful semantic fix: the request frame now targets one service and gets forwarded so siblings can react. The data shape is mostly right. Main concern is putting a live FrameProcessor on the frame instead of an id or name — control frames travel best as flat, comparable, loggable data. Identity comparison via `==` is also fragile; `is` or id-equality would be clearer. Overall SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE with one WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE smell on the service field.
